title: Improving the time-horizon dependence of temporal maximum flow
formal: Can exact maximum flow over T explicitly given snapshots, with zero transit time and unlimited storage, be computed with a capacity-independent arithmetic-operation bound P(n,m)T^(5/2−δ) for some fixed polynomial P and constant δ>0? Yes: the source’s own expansion and the established O(NM) static maximum-flow bound give O(n(m+n)T²).
why: Historically asks whether the time horizon forces the high exponent obtained from a small selection of static algorithms. The positive resolution illustrates why temporal-flow complexity must be assessed against the strongest applicable static bounds and with the arithmetic cost model made explicit.
status_note: Checked 11 September 2026. The question of beating the listed T^(5/2) factor is already answered by the strongly polynomial O(NM) static bound of Orlin (STOC 2013) combined with the exact time expansion explicitly supplied by the 2021 source. The resulting bound is O(n(m+n)T²) arithmetic operations. The theorem/model match was checked; this is not an independent proof audit or a proof-assistant solution certification.

progress.text: Orlin’s STOC result establishes the static O(NM) maximum-flow bound, together with the earlier dense-graph bound.
The seminar compares a limited set of static algorithms and asks whether the resulting T^(5/2) dependence can be improved.

references.title: Max flows in O(nm) time, or better
references.locator: STOC 2013, pp. 765–774; checked manuscript revised 25 July 2012. Abstract, introduction and Section 2 read. The strongly polynomial O(nm) bound combines Orlin’s sparse-graph result with the earlier King–Rao–Tarjan dense-graph result. Integer capacities may include infinity; finite rational capacities can be scaled without altering the arithmetic-operation bound.

sentences: The problem concerns exact flow through a known sequence of capacitated graph snapshots with zero transit time and unlimited storage.
The source asks whether its listed T^(5/2) dependence on the time horizon can be improved.
Its exact layered representation has O(nT) vertices and O((m+n)T) arcs.
The older strongly polynomial static maximum-flow bound gives O(n(m+n)T²) arithmetic operations on that network.
The numerical improvement question is therefore resolved positively and is separate from finding the optimal temporal-flow complexity.

upgraded_from.title: Minimal complexity of MaxFlow on dynamic graphs

definitions: The input has a fixed vertex set V with n≥2 vertices, distinct source s and sink t, and snapshots G₁,…,G_T on V for an integer T≥1. There are at most m possible ordered arcs, with a nonnegative rational capacity c_τ(e) at each time τ; absent arcs have capacity zero. The full snapshot/capacity table is explicit. Arc traversal takes zero time, so flow may cross several arcs in the same snapshot; it may wait at intermediate vertices between snapshots with no storage bound. Flow starts at s and the objective is the total amount arriving at t by time T. More formally, its value is the maximum static flow in the layered network with vertices (v,τ), a super-source S and super-sink Z, capacity-c_τ(u,v) arcs (u,τ)→(v,τ), infinite-capacity storage arcs (v,τ)→(v,τ+1) for intermediate v and τ<T, and infinite-capacity arcs S→(s,τ) and (t,τ)→Z. Static flow is nonnegative, satisfies arc capacities and conservation at every vertex other than S,Z, and maximizes net outflow from S. The layered network has N=nT+2 vertices and M=O((m+n)T) arcs. Its artificial infinite capacities can equivalently be replaced by one plus the sum of all finite input capacities. The source compares numbers of arithmetic operations independently of capacity magnitudes, rather than bit operations on unrestricted-size numerators. Rational capacities are interpreted in this standard strongly polynomial arithmetic convention: common-denominator scaling preserves the operation-count bound and the answer rescales. The comparison concerns an offline temporal network supplied in full, not online insertions and deletions in a maintained graph. P and δ must be independent of all instance parameters.
answer_criterion: Give an exact algorithm with the stated uniformly improved time-horizon exponent, under the source’s capacity-independent arithmetic convention, or rule one out. The established bound O(n(m+n)T²) supplies the positive answer with δ=1/2. This does not claim to determine the optimal dependence on every graph parameter.

context_blocks.title: Time order can create routes absent from any one snapshot
context_blocks.text: If the only arc at time one is s→v and the only arc at time two is v→t, both with unit capacity, one unit can reach the sink by waiting at v. Reversing those two snapshots makes that transfer impossible. Unlimited storage preserves flow for later use but does not move it backward in time.

context_blocks.title: The historical question compared a limited list of algorithms
context_blocks.text: The seminar’s table contains classical augmenting-path and preflow algorithms. Applied to the layered graph, most have a T³ factor and the best listed one has T^(5/2). The table is explicitly incomplete, so its best entry is not a lower bound or a complete account of known static maximum-flow algorithms.

context_blocks.title: A known bound already gives a smaller exponent
context_blocks.text: The static O(NM) theorem applied to the source’s N=nT+2 and M=O((m+n)T) expansion yields O(n(m+n)T²). For the source’s simplifying convention n=O(m), this becomes O(nmT²). The theorem predates the seminar and answers the numerical question without imposing a special capacity bound.

context_blocks.title: What the resolution does and does not classify
context_blocks.text: The improvement settles whether the T^(5/2) factor in that comparison can be beaten. It does not establish a matching lower bound for temporal maximum flow, nor a new algorithm for online dynamic maintenance. Those broader questions were not the precise numerical target of the contribution.
